evidence_requests.question: Screen the current partition for unsupported internal splits and weak pair boundaries.

observations.meaning: Algorithmic eigengap screening resolution for each candidate set; candidate_k=1 means the dominant spectral gap is at the single-cluster resolution.
observations.finding: All six candidate sets (K6_C0001–K6_C0006) screen at candidate_k=1, so the partition-level screen shows no dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal in any candidate.

observations.meaning: Magnitude of the leading spectral gap at the single-cluster resolution for each candidate set.

observations.meaning: Profile of spectral gaps across candidate resolutions for each set.
observations.finding: In every set the first gap is an order of magnitude larger than subsequent gaps, indicating the single-cluster resolution dominates; no secondary gap of comparable magnitude appears.

observations.meaning: Average fused affinity among patients assigned to the same candidate set.
observations.finding: Within-set affinities are tightly clustered (≈0.0095–0.0102) across all six sets, showing comparable internal cohesion at the partition level.

observations.meaning: Relatively close candidate pairs and their between-set affinity; a pair-review entry point, not a merge conclusion.
observations.finding: The closest boundaries are K6_C0001–K6_C0004 (0.00924) and K6_C0002–K6_C0003 (0.00922), with the remaining listed pairs slightly lower (≈0.0090–0.0091). These between-set affinities are close to the within-set affinities, so the listed pairs are relatively weakly separated boundaries flagged for possible pair review.

observations.meaning: Number of patients represented in the structural calculation for each candidate set.
observations.finding: All six sets are represented by 14–21 patients, so the structural calculations cover the full partition membership.

evidence_reports.dimension_interpretation: This partition-level structural diagnostic is triage evidence about whether current membership or boundary is expressed in the fused patient geometry.
